## Overview

The ISO C++ committee, known as WG21, met in Búzios, Brazil from 16 to 21 November to work through the international comments that sank C++26's first approval ballot. According to [Herb Sutter's trip report](https://herbsutter.com/2026/11/21/c26-is-done-again-trip-report-november-2026-iso-c-standards-meeting-buzios-brazil/), "C++26 technical work, originally completed in March, was reopened and is now recompleted: The anticipated plan is to reissue the updated C++26 document for a s...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (804 words, within the 400-1200 range) with distinct Overview, event, comparison, next-steps and 'What We Don't Know' sections. Neutral, procedural tone throughout; no editorializing or sensationalism. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both manifest snapshots fetched cleanly (HTTP 200, no archive_fallback, suspicious_patterns: null on both). sha256 of each decompressed .html.gz matches the manifest exactly (source-0: 5b38dec4...90e6e1; source-1: 87c8a4e9...608e14). Read both full HTML->text extractions directly from disk (sources/2026-11/wg21-reaffirms-contracts-in-c26-at-bzios-adopts-an-always-enforced-label-heads-to-a-new-dis-ballot/source-0.html.gz [herbsutter.com, 'Sutter's Mill' trip report] and source-1.html.gz [train-it.eu blog Part 7 by Mateusz Pusz]). Quote-by-quote audit of all 11 quoted spans in the submission against the raw extracted text: 10 of 11 are exact verbatim matches (the title/summary/lead vote tally '111 in favor, 9 opposed, and 8 abstaining' is independently present verbatim in BOTH source-0 line 60 and source-1 lines 13-14, confirming the writer's cross-corroboration claim; the P4451R2 'Early Adoption of an Always-Enforced Label' attribution to Joshua Berne matches source-0 line 68 verbatim; the historical vote tallies 100/14/12 (Feb 2025, 87.7%) and 114/12/3 (March 2026, 90.5%) and the Búzios 111/9/8 (92.5%) percentages are all stated directly by Sutter in source-0 lines 42-50/60, not merely derived by the writer). ISSUE FOUND: Quote #2, attributed to Pusz as verbatim -- 'Contracts remain in the C++26 draft after the WG 21 meeting in Búzios, Brazil on November 17, 2026.' -- is NOT a verbatim quote. Source-1 line 8 actually reads as two separate sentences: 'Contracts remain in the C++26 draft.' followed by a new sentence, 'On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, at the WG 21 meeting in Búzios, Brazil, a plenary poll to remove them didn't reach consensus.' The submission stitched the first clause to a prepositional phrase lifted from the second sentence and presented the combination inside quote marks as if Pusz wrote it that way. The underlying fact (contracts remained in the draft; the Nov 17, 2026 Búzios plenary removal poll did not reach consensus) is accurate and fully supported by the source -- this is a quote-fidelity problem, not a fabricated fact, and it sits in the Overview/lead paragraph. Filed as a corrections record (src/content/corrections/2026-11/24-wg21-reaffirms-contracts-in-c26-at-bzios-adopts-an-always-enforced-label-heads-to-a-new-dis-ballot.json) rather than REJECT, because the fact itself is true and the correction can honestly inform readers without gutting the lead. Follow-up/duplicate check: verified both prior Herald articles this submission references actually exist and say what is attributed to them -- src/content/articles/2026-11/05-c26-fails-its-iso-dis-ballot-... (confirms 'failed its DIS ballot in October', exact text 'C++26... failed its Draft International Standard (DIS) ballot in October') and src/content/articles/2026-11/14-herb-sutters-paper-argues-stroustrups-objection-... (confirms 'Mateusz Pusz, who writes that he is a member of the Polish national body and prefers to keep contracts' -- the basis for this submission's 'Pusz, a member of the Polish national body' framing, which the current train-it.eu snapshot itself does not restate but which was independently verified in the prior, already-published review). This submission reports genuinely new information -- the Búzios meeting's actual outcome (contracts retained, P4451R2 always-enforced label adopted, 111-9-8 reship vote, comparison to the Feb 2025 and March 2026 votes, next-steps to a new DIS ballot) -- not a re-narration of the Oct ballot-failure or Nov 14 Stroustrup-paper stories. Claim-accuracy absence/quantifier checks: confirmed source-0 (herbsutter.com) contains no breakdown of the Tuesday removal-poll vote count (grep for '41' returns zero hits in source-0, while it appears in source-1 as 'For Against Abstain 41 90 20'), matching the article's 'Sutter's report does not break out the Tuesday removal poll by vote count, so that figure is reported here on Pusz's account alone.' Confirmed neither source states an exact open/close date for the new DIS ballot (only 'eight weeks' duration in source-1), matching the article's absence claim. Confirmed neither source mentions 'C++27' naming for the Búzios outcome, matching the article's absence claim -- the C++27-naming background itself traces correctly to the Nov 5 Herald article's sourcing of WG21 Direction Group member Daveed Vandevoorde via Pusz. Anthropic disclosure: not required - story is ISO C++ standards-committee procedure; no mention of Anthropic, Claude, or an Anthropic-operated product in the headline/summary/lead or anywhere in the body.

The single issue is the Quote #2 quote-fidelity problem described above, now covered by a corrections record. No orphan source URLs: both article.sources URLs (herbsutter.com trip report, train-it.eu blog) are the only two URLs cited in body_markdown besides internal Herald cross-links, and both are correctly listed in article.sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and procedural throughout; attributes competing framings (Sutter's vs. Pusz's) without adopting either; explicitly flags what remains unknown in its own section.
editor_notes.originality: New development in an ongoing Herald-tracked story (Oct 2026 DIS ballot failure -> Nov 14 Stroustrup-paper analysis -> this Nov 24 report on the Búzios meeting's resolution). Not a duplicate; no overlapping recent coverage found of the Búzios outcome specifically.
concerns: Quote #2 (Pusz, Overview paragraph) splices two separate source sentences into one string presented as a verbatim quotation; the underlying fact is accurate but the quotation itself is not verbatim. Corrected via corrections record rather than REJECT because it does not change the substance of the lead.
recommendations: Future submissions quoting train-it.eu or herbsutter.com should paraphrase (without quote marks) when combining material from adjacent sentences, reserving quote marks strictly for single, contiguous verbatim spans.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, substantively new report on the Búzios WG21 meeting's outcome, correctly cross-corroborating the 111-9-8 vote across two independent accounts and correctly carrying forward verified context from the Herald's own prior coverage. One isolated quote-fidelity issue (not a fabricated fact) is addressed via a corrections record. herbsutter.com added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review (confirmed via the site's own byline 'Published by Herb Sutter' and author bio stating he served as chair of the ISO C++ standards committee 2002-2025 and is the designer/co-designer of ISO C++ language features -- a legitimate, credentialed individual-expert blog, not sponsored content). Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate follow-up reporting on a developing ISO C++ standards story for a defined developer audience; procedural subject matter, not broad-audience news.
